title_candidates: Hugging Face and NVIDIA put agent data under a microscope
summary: A new Hugging Face/NVIDIA post argues that open data matters for agents, and points readers to a visual atlas for inspecting Nemotron post-training prompts.

primary_source.title: Data for Agents
primary_source.author: Hugging Face and NVIDIA
key_facts: Hugging Face and NVIDIA published a post explaining why agent behavior depends on data, not just model weights.
The post argues that agents need data covering tool-use failures, multi-step workflows, retrieval, safety, user simulation, and recovery from broken calls.
NVIDIA says the Nemotron open data effort includes trillions of pre-training tokens and millions of post-training samples.
The post links to a Nemotron Post-Training v3 Prompt Atlas that lets people inspect prompt samples by domain, dataset, pipeline stage, and tool use.
The authors warn that synthetic data still needs lineage, grounding, review, and clear documentation.

prerequisites: Optional Hugging Face account for deeper dataset access

steps.instruction: Open the Nemotron Prompt Atlas and wait for the visualization to load.
Search for a domain you care about, such as coding, safety, math, or tool use.
Open several nearby samples and note whether they look like real tasks, synthetic tasks, or mixed traces.
Write down one behavior you would want an agent to handle, then check whether the samples cover success and failure cases.
Use that checklist when judging any agent demo: ask what data shaped the behavior, not just what benchmark it claims.

risk_flags: This is more conceptual than consumer-product news, so the guide focuses on inspecting the public atlas.
